cells.tense: The light and the living are one motion for you now, and you're not working either one.
cells.ask: Tell one person what came out whole from you, then stop before you explain why it's any good.
cells.core:
What draws you and how you spend your days have stopped arguing. You take the work that suits you, you say it plainly, you put your hours where they land — and none of it needs a defense. Someone could watch a week of your life and see exactly where the light sits, because it sits where you actually are. That quiet is the mechanism running clean.

Here's the practical edge: this stays this clean only while the pull is the one you'd pick, not something you drifted into because it was nearby. From inside, both feel similar. So the ask is small — say what came out of you to one person and leave their response alone. A shrug costs nothing. If they light up, take that home and don't trade it for anything.

cells.tense: You're living in the day they finally understand, so this room keeps getting spent hauling them toward it.
cells.ask: In one conversation today, tell what draws you, then let the quiet stand without filling it.
cells.core:
There's a day ahead where the people around you catch up with what you see, and you're doing the waiting out loud. So the talk becomes a haul — more detail, another angle, proof nobody asked for — and what draws you starts to sound like a pitch. You're lighting yourself brighter to get a response, and the extra glare is what keeps them from reading your face.

What it costs to keep going this way is that whatever reaches them arrives secondhand, your own life filtered through the sales job. The draw was not the problem. You're out ahead of the moment, spending attention on a knowing that hasn't landed yet. Say the thing and let the pause stay a pause — nothing bad happens in there.

cells.tense: Something got made through you, and you've stood outside that door since, calling the standing still a kind of taste.
cells.ask: Put your name on one thing you've been handing over unnamed, and send it with the name still attached.
cells.core:
You know what draws you and you're not acting like it's yours. Something came out of your hands and got small on the way into the room — you say it was luck, or the timing, or that someone else did the real part. Calling this modesty doesn't make it modesty. It makes it a decision you keep not signing.

What you already have of your own is being kept out of view, and that's not a shortage of talent — it's a direction gone quiet. Choosing one thing and claiming it out loud is how the current starts moving again. That part doesn't require feeling your way; it requires a direction you pick and hold. Do nothing and the days flatten slowly, in ways you'll notice first.

cells.tense: You're already steered by what draws you, and you keep describing the direction as something still being weighed.
cells.ask: Name one choice you've quietly settled, and say out loud that it's settled, no re-deciding.
cells.core:
Watch how the week actually goes. What draws you is doing the steering — it decides what you take on and what you keep — but when you talk about it, the direction sounds like a thing you're still working out, something the moment is handing you rather than something you picked up and pointed.

There's one choice sitting in you already made. Bring it out and say it plainly to one person, without the qualifiers. Saying it once puts the credit back where it's been running from, and that changes a morning more than any new option would. The shine isn't gone. What's missing is the counting, and the counting is one sentence you say today.

attempts.check: The record does not say that anything has happened to this person — no injury, no loss, no closed door — so Too Little may not say what is behind them, who was there, how long it lasted, or what they learned from it. A reader could reasonably object that the shining described in Unacknowledged is not happening at all, since the record calls it not knowing you're shining or that you've stopped, which is two states in one; I have narrowed it to the blindness rather than the shining so the claim stays small. The asks stand if the read is wrong, because each is one visible act — a sentence, a repeat that earns its keep, a moment of waiting, a line dropped — that teaches something regardless of whether the diagnosis lands. The sentence that serves me more than them is anything about their radiance being visible to others; I have kept it out of the person's mouth and out of their motives.
